newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: British royal yacht Britannia arrives in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: British royal yacht Britannia arrives in Singapore.

text.p: The British royal yacht Britannia arrived in Singapore on Tuesday as part of its last official voyage before being decommissioned.

Sailing into Singapore harbour to the tune of a Royal Marines band and with ceremonial flags flying, the elegant mini-liner docked at a wharf close to the financial district where it will be used as the base for British business events.
Britannia, home to Queen Elizabeth on overseas visits, is due to be taken out of service after the current tour, ending 44 years afloat.
The 6,000-tonne luxury yacht costs about 10 million pounds ($16 million) a year to run, and with a crew of 236, is considered inefficient by modern standards.
While in Singapore, Britannia will be used for a series of receptions to promote British business interests.
Britannia leaves Singapore on April 18 and will sail on to several other Asian cities before reaching Hong Kong in June.
Heir to the British throne Prince Charles will sail out of Hong Kong a few minutes after midnight on July 1, when the territory is handed back to China.
